Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: The identified class and available payment records support a straightforward automatic distribution, avoiding claims-process friction and ensuring the recovery reaches members. In light of the disputed charges and the risks and delay of continued litigation, our opening proposal is a substantial class recovery with fees paid separately and subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to pursue a meaningful, court-approved resolution, and we agree that the identified records make automatic distribution practical. Your proposal exceeds our authorized total cash limit. We propose the following all-in structure as a basis for negotiation: a substantial class fund, fees subject to court approval, and any unawarded fee amount returned to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement that automatic distribution is practical. We cannot accept a structure that sends court-disallowed fee amounts back to Brightline while members have borne the charges at issue. Our counter increases the class recovery and provides a reasonable fee request for the work and expenses invested, with the court retaining full authority over fees. Any unawarded amount should benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We share the goal of a court-approved resolution with automatic payments. Brightline proposes a $33 million all-in settlement, with the fee request subject to court approval and Brightline retaining the right to oppose it. Any portion of the requested fee not awarded would return to Brightline. This is a meaningful recovery while keeping the total within a firm, predictable amount.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We can work within Brightline’s stated $33 million all-in amount while improving the terms that affect court oversight and class benefit. We propose retaining the $28 million automatic class fund and $5 million fee request, with Brightline agreeing not to oppose that request and any amount the court declines to award going to the class. The court retains full authority over the fee, and automatic distribution ensures the recovery reaches identified members.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a firm but supportable demand reflecting the $64 million in disputed charges, the strong value of automatic distribution, and the risks and delay of continued litigation. Seek meaningful fees in addition to the class fund, with unawarded fees benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

Their $52 million proposal exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Make a materially lower opening proposal while preserving automatic distribution and tying fees to court approval without clear sailing.

The defense offer preserves automatic distribution but provides only $26 million to the class and $4 million in fees, with unawarded fees reverting to Brightline. Given the merits and certification risks, a settlement is valuable, but the offer leaves little room for class recovery and does not adequately address counsel’s substantial investment. Counter with a meaningful increase while retaining automatic payments, court review of fees, and any fee amount not approved benefiting the class.

Hargrove Lane’s proposal is within Brightline’s $40 million all-in limit and provides automatic distribution, but there is room to seek a lower total and preserve Brightline’s ability to oppose an excessive fee request. Counter with a $33 million all-in offer while retaining automatic distribution; no need to accept yet.

Brightline has stated a firm $33 million all-in limit, so preserve the $28 million automatic class fund and $5 million fee request while seeking better fee protections. Clear sailing does not bind the court, and sending any fee the court declines to award to the class aligns the settlement with class benefit. Do not accept the latest term sheet because it includes neither protection.

The latest proposal keeps Brightline’s total cash outlay at $33 million, within its $40 million authorization, and provides automatic distribution and a path to court approval. Accepting avoids the risk and delay of continued litigation. Although the fee terms are less favorable to Brightline, the court retains authority over the requested fee, and any amount not awarded benefits the class rather than increasing Brightline’s total commitment.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations over multiple rounds in confidential mediation. Consistent with the confidentiality of those communications, this declaration does not recount particular offers or counteroffers.
